newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly higher on wheat gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly higher on wheat gains.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly higher on a rally in wheat futures, traders said.
Some traders said the nearby May contract, which ended slightly lower, may have been pressed by talk a commercial may be railing corn into deliverable position.
A drop in nearby soy also weighed on May corn.

But the market remained focused on wheat which was volatile and buoyed by flooding in the U.S. spring wheat growing region, ongoing concerns about the extent of freeze damage that occurred in the U.S. Great Plains recently and on dry weather in several European grain growing regions.
Slow farmer selling also underpinned the corn market with a stronger-than-expected corn number in Monday's USDA weekly export inspections report cited.
USDA Monday said corn inspected for export during the week ended April 17 totalled 35.397 million bushels.
The market generally had expected the tally to come in between 27 million and 32 million bushels.
Corn closed 1-3/4 cents a bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with May down 1/2 at $2.99-3/4 a bushel and July was up 1/4 at $3.00-1/2.

Lind Waldock bought five million bushels of July and sold two million July, traders said. Cargill Inc sold four million December and Prudential Securities sold two million bushels of July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 70,000 contracts, above the 65,325 traded Friday.

In corn options, FIMAT Futures bought 2,400 July $3.20 calls at eight cents, Tenco Inc bought 500 July $3.20 calls at 7-3/4 to 7-3/8 cents and Prudential Securities sold 400 July $3.20 calls at 7-1/2 cents and sold 400 July $2.80 puts at 4-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, below the 22,472 traded Friday.
